sentences.english_text: The dancing girls were next.
There were twelve of them and they wore beautiful costumes with ribbons and spangles.
Grippy stood at the side of the stage, watching them, enjoying the dancing and the music.
I'm so glad that I didn't listen to Mr. Wind.
If I had stayed on that park bench as he told me to, I wouldn't be starring in my own show now.
The dancers were doing very fancy steps.
Grippy moved forward to get a better look.
And as he did, one of the dancers kicked him high into the air and Grippy flew into the orchestra pit.
Where the orchestra was playing.
He landed on a trombone.
Now a trombone is an instrument that slides in and out.
And Grippy found himself being shoved back and forth as the trombonist played.
Grippy hung on as hard as he could.
But the trombone was smooth and Grippy was flung into the air, down inside of the tuba.
It was like a giant slide going down and down and the music was so loud in Grippy's ears that he thought he was going to go deaf.
Oompa, oompa, the tuba said.
And each time the musician played into it, the air pushed Grippy up.
Oompa, oompa, and Grippy went up again.
The music was so loud that he thought he was going to go deaf.
Again.
The musician played a deep note that blew Grippy out of the tuba onto the piano.
The piano player played very fast and Grippy found himself thrown all over the keyboard.
He was unable to get his balance.
When the musician hit a heavy chord, Grippy was flung into the air again onto the bow of a violin.
The violinist moved the bow back and forth and Grippy tried desperately to hang on.
He was not strong enough and he flew back onto the stage and landed on the foot of a dancer.
The dancer was doing high kicks and Grippy found himself hurtling through the air.
He went up, up, up, then down, down, down.
He landed backstage on the back of a very strange looking animal.
The musician played a very loud, very loud note that blew Grippy out of the tuba.
